text:
Jordan: FYI — inbound from Acme Corp (enterprise) with console/observability asks. They want:
- Per-route & per-team cost breakdowns (token-level attribution)
- Daily CSV export for chargeback system
- Trace->request linking (trace ids surfaced in console)
- Per-model cost by route + SLA ops metrics
Context: legal/procurement wants this by end of quarter to finalize contract. Can product triage? cc @Mia :eyes:

Sam: Acme is on Dedicated, runs ~150M tokens/day across ~20 teams. They need daily per-team totals to feed their finance system. Deal at risk if we can't provide a reliable CSV export + basic per-route splits. They asked for a minimal ship vs full UI.
Key requested CSV schema: date, team, route, model, tokens_input, tokens_output, token_cost, total_cost

Mia: Thanks — proposed triage and scope: 
- MVP (P0): CSV export of daily aggregates per (team,route,model). Acceptance: CSV matches schema above, can be downloaded or S3-delivered.
- P1: Expose trace_id on request detail page and link to traces/logs.
- P2: Add per-model breakdown in Console UI and API.
Questions for eng: retention window for raw request events? cardinality concerns? can we reuse existing cost pipeline?
I'll open an intake ticket and schedule a scoping call today.

Alex: Engineering notes / constraints:
- Cardinality: team+route+model quickly multiplies; need unique route counts (how many routes per customer) to size storage/aggregation.
- Computation point: online attribution at request time vs offline batch join. Online is exact but adds CPU per request; offline needs raw events + join to billing rates.
- Storage: request-level retention for 90d is heavy. Aggregated daily sums are cheap and generally satisfy chargeback needs.
- Suggestion for MVP: compute attribution at ingestion and emit daily aggregates per (customer,team,route,model) into metrics store; CSV export from aggregates. Rough effort: 2-3 sprints end-to-end + UI.

Jordan: Example of current request event we ingest (for reference):
{
  "request_id": "req_abc123",
  "customer_id": "acme",
  "route": "/summarize/v2",
  "team": "content-marketing",
  "model": "rw-medium",
  "tokens_in": 126,
  "tokens_out": 430,
  "timestamp": "2025-11-03T14:22:11Z"
}
We also have a kafka topic `requests.events` where these are produced. For Acme specifically: ~25k unique routes but ~90% traffic on top ~40 routes.

Mia: Proposed immediate plan:
- Create intake ticket for CSV MVP (daily aggregates -> S3 export + UI link)
- Scoping call today 3pm PT with Eng + Support + Sales
- Acceptance criteria for MVP: CSV schema as above, export runs daily, accuracy within 1% for token counts, docs + sample script for customer to ingest CSV
I'll assign Alex + Jordan to the intake ticket. If we can get a working prototype in 2 weeks, Sales can demo to Acme while UI/trace work continues.

observability-bot: Intake ticket created: PROD-6581 — Console: per-team daily cost CSV export — assignees: Alex, Jordan — link: https://redwood/boards/PROD-6581

Sam: +1. I'll notify Acme that we have a scoping call and that CSV MVP is prioritized. If procurement pushes for timeline I'll escalate to account execs. :thumbsup:

Mia: Thanks all — marking this as intake -> product backlog. See you on the scoping call.
